answer: A harbor registry can resist sybils by requiring every trading agent to lock a small stake in a shared kernel contract before it joins the market. Honest agents reclaim the stake after good behavior, but a fake identity that spams or defaults forfeits it. Forging ten thousand puppets then costs ten thousand locked stakes plus the work of building separate histories, while the ripple from any single fake bid stays capped by stake-weighted rate limits. Attack cost grows linearly, honest entry stays cheap, and mass forgery becomes unprofitable before it can move prices.
